items.definition:
to move to a lower rank or position
He was demoted after failing to meet his targets.

to decorate food; to seize wages
She decided to garnish the soup with fresh parsley.

to make a sound quieter
She tried to muffle her laughter with her hand.

to fill something up again
We need to replenish our supplies.

snipe (to shoot at someone from a hidden position; to make a sly or petty verbal attack)
The critics continued to snipe at the director's latest film.

spew (to expel large quantities of something rapidly and forcibly)
The volcano began to spew ash and lava into the air.

symbolize (to be a symbol of; represent)
The dove is often used to symbolize peace.

to treat someone cruelly or unfairly
The scammer tried to victimize elderly people.

to astonish or overwhelm
The complexity of the problem made his mind boggle.

to displace a bone from its joint; to disrupt
He fell and managed to dislocate his shoulder.

to understand wrongly
It's easy to misinterpret someone's intentions if you don't know them well.

to adapt to modern needs or habits
The company plans to modernize its old equipment.

To subject to pressure.
The cabin of the airplane is pressurized for comfort.

To emit (energy, especially light or heat) in the form of rays or waves.
The sun radiates heat and light.

to cancel a subscription
You can unsubscribe from our newsletter at any time.

to put forward (an idea or theory) as a hypothesis
Scientists hypothesize that life may exist on other planets.

to make someone extremely angry
His constant interruptions began to infuriate her.

to separate; to examine thoroughly
She had to sift through a lot of information to find the truth.

to suffocate; to cover completely
She tried to smother the flames with a blanket.

to change direction suddenly
The car suddenly veered off the road.

to dry up and decay
Without water, the plants will wither.

to shorten (a book, movie, etc.) without losing the sense
The editor decided to abridge the novel for younger readers.

to argue about petty things
The children would often bicker over toys.

to attract and hold the attention of
Her performance managed to captivate the entire audience.

to make or enact laws
Parliament will legislate on the new policy next month.

to settle or lie comfortably within or against something
The cat loved to nestle in her owner's lap.

perform better than
The company managed to outperform its competitors this quarter.

sell goods, especially small articles, by going from place to place
He used to peddle newspapers on the street corner.

pierce and make a hole or holes in
The machine is designed to perforate the paper for easy tearing.

drive back (an attack or attacker) by force
The defenders managed to repulse the enemy attack.

To place on a shelf; to postpone or put aside
They decided to shelve the project until next year.

To become less intense, violent, or severe
The floodwaters began to subside after the heavy rain.

To provoke or challenge someone with insulting remarks
The bullies would often taunt him about his new glasses.

to descend from a vehicle; to land on something
A bird alighted on the branch.

to set aside for a specific purpose
The government earmarked funds for the new project.

to enclose or cover
The ancient artifact was encased in glass.

to rise and fall irregularly
The temperature can fluctuate wildly in the desert.

to make something appear larger
The microscope can magnify tiny objects.

to put an end to; cancel
The boss decided to nix the proposal.

to defeat or overcome with superior strength
The guards managed to overpower the intruder.

to restore (someone) to health or normal life through training and therapy after imprisonment, addiction, or illness
The program aims to rehabilitate offenders.

To suppress or prevent something from happening.
She tried to stifle a yawn during the long meeting.

To undergo great mental anguish; to struggle with.
She agonized over the decision for days.

to establish a colony in
European powers sought to colonize new lands.

to do without; to give up
I decided to forgo dessert to stick to my diet.

To appear or become visible; to happen or come into being.
The ghost seemed to materialize out of thin air.

to cook by simmering in a small amount of liquid; to hunt or catch illegally
She likes to poach salmon for a light dinner.

to fasten with a rivet; to engross
The workers will rivet the metal plates together to secure them.

to clean thoroughly; to search thoroughly
We had to scour the entire house for the lost keys.

tell someone about a secret or private matter while trusting them not to repeat it to others
She decided to confide her worries in her best friend.

to make someone unable to hear, either temporarily or permanently
The loud explosion deafened him for a few minutes.

to charge with electricity; to thrill or excite
The news of the victory electrified the crowd.

to flow out in a rapid and plentiful stream; to express admiration effusively
Water began to gush from the broken pipe.

to connect or engage with each other by overlapping or fitting together
The gears interlock to make the machine work.

to make ineffective; nullify
The new evidence seemed to negate the previous findings.

to analyze (a sentence) into its component parts and describe their syntactic roles; to analyze (something, such as a series of observations) to discover its implications or meaning
It's difficult to parse the meaning of such a complex sentence.

to insert punctuation marks; to interrupt at intervals
Remember to punctuate your sentences correctly.

to wander or travel without a fixed destination
The sheep were allowed to rove freely across the hills.

to enjoy (food or drink) with relish; to appreciate fully
She savored every bite of the delicious meal.

to send sexually explicit messages or images by cell phone
It is illegal to sext someone under the age of consent.

To move or act in an awkward or clumsy way.
He tends to bumble around the kitchen, making a mess.

arrive at (a fact or a conclusion) by reasoning; draw as a logical conclusion.
From the evidence, we can deduce that he was the culprit.

To give a false or misleading account of.
The politician was accused of trying to misrepresent the facts.

To make necessary.
The new regulations will necessitate changes in our production process.
